title: Request for clip-level metadata to reproduce the dataset
body:
Dear Zikai and Prof. Yin,

I'm working on reproducing the GLARE listening-head dataset for benchmarking use. Thank you for releasing the reaction-annotation pipeline and the processed annotations; they've been very helpful.

To align exactly with your benchmark, I'm trying to reconstruct the listener clips from the original RealTalk / Seamless Interaction sources. I understand the source licenses prevent redistributing raw or cropped frames. However, the released annotations (the reaction CSVs and MediaPipe .pkl files) index frame_index from 0 within each clip, with no mapping back to the source video, so the clip boundaries can't be recovered from them.

Could you share the per-clip text metadata that defines the clips? Ideally, for each clip_id:

1. video_id
2. start_frame and end_frame in the source video (the key item, this lets us cut the exact segments)
3. speaker / listener assignment (e.g. p0 / p1)
4. crop bounding box (x, y, w, h) and the first-valid-frame index (to match your Face-Alignment crop)

Even just the (video_id, start_frame, end_frame, listener) mapping would let us reproduce the clips faithfully and avoid discrepancies from re-running diarization and detection locally. If you have the "usable" manifest from your pipeline, that would be perfect.

Thank you for your time and for contributing this work to the community.

Best regards,
Laxmi Narayen N V

title: Request for pretrained GLARE checkpoint release
body:
Hi, thank you for releasing the code for GLARE, and congratulations on the NeurIPS 2026 acceptance!

I'm interested in reproducing the results and trying out listening-head generation with the model. However, I couldn't find the trained GLARE checkpoint in the repository or the Releases section. The inference example in the README uses `--ckpt_path /path/to/glare_checkpoint.pth`, but no download link seems to be provided.

Since training from scratch requires curating and preprocessing the RealTalk and Seamless Interaction datasets (plus a 4-GPU setup for 650 epochs), having access to the pretrained weights would be very helpful for the community.

Would you be able to share the trained GLARE checkpoint (e.g., via Hugging Face or Google Drive)? 

If you plan to release it later, could you share a rough timeline?

Thanks again for your great work!
